newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak c.bank says ready to support SKK if needed.
newsitem.headline: Slovak c.bank says ready to support SKK if needed.

text.p: The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) said on Thursday that it was ready to move quickly to support the Slovak crown if the situation gets "out of control".

"We are following the Czech development very closely, and the Slovak crown is under control at the moment, but we are ready to quickly react and support it if it gets out of control," NBS Treasury Director Frantisek Szulenyi said.
The Slovak crown weakened by some 40 basis points in nervous afternoon trading on Thursday to around -0.70 percent versus its mark/dollar basket parity.
The Czech crown plunged about one percent in early Thursday trading before the Czech central bank intervened on the market to boost the ailing currency.
Szulenyi would not say at what levels the NBS saw it neccessary to support the Slovak crown, nor would he disclose what tools would the bank use if the intervention was needed.
"There are some signals that we can expect stronger pressure on the Slovak crown in the near future, involving larger volumes than we have seen so far," he said.
Traders estimated that up to $100 million has left the country so far today as market volatility increased.
Traders say foreign players are trading the Czech and Slovak crowns together, effectively implying a depreciation trend on both currencies.
Some dealers said they expected the Slovak crown to weaken further during the day and that it could even test the 1.0 percent level on the depreciation side of the currency basket midpoint.

Szulenyi said the NBS so far did not need to directly intervene on the market to support the Slovak crown, but that an indirect intervention through its fixing helped the crown stay steady two weeks ago.
On Thursday the NBS fixed the crown some 45 basis points above the market levels, and some dealers said this could be seen as a signal that the central bank does not want the crown to fall too much.
